title: Exponential lower bounds for unrestricted threshold-of-threshold circuits
formal: Does there exist an explicit Boolean function family \((f_n)_{n\geq1}\), in the source’s sense \(\mathrm{NP}\), and constants \(c>0\) and \(n_0\), such that every unrestricted depth-two threshold circuit computing \(f_n\) has at least \(2^{cn}\) gates for every \(n\geq n_0\)?
why: Depth-two threshold circuits are a basic model of two layers of weighted Boolean decisions. An exponential lower bound with unrestricted real weights would establish a strong limit on this expressive shallow architecture for an explicitly verifiable computational task.
status_note: The source states this challenge as open. The source-wide explicitness convention and circuit model were rechecked on 13 September 2026, together with the abstract of Chen’s subsequent work and a limited later-work search. No unconditional resolution was verified; this is not an exhaustive status review, and status remains source_open.

progress.text: The book distinguishes unrestricted gate count from weight-restricted lower bounds and poses the exponential depth-two question as Research Problem 11.40.
Chen gives conditional implications toward superpolynomial depth-two threshold lower bounds. The checked abstract does not establish an unconditional solution.

sentences: A threshold gate decides whether a weighted sum of Boolean inputs reaches a specified threshold.
This question asks for an NP function family requiring exponentially many gates in every two-layer threshold circuit.
All weights are unrestricted real numbers, and size counts gates rather than their weights.
The book’s definition of explicitness means a uniform polynomial-time verifier, while known bounds with extra weight restrictions do not settle this target.
A resolution would reveal a strong computational limitation of two layers of weighted decisions.

definitions: A threshold gate on Boolean inputs \(z_1,\ldots,z_t\) outputs one if and only if \(\sum_{i=1}^{t}w_i z_i\geq\theta\), where all weights \(w_i\) and the threshold \(\theta\) are arbitrary real numbers of either sign. An unrestricted depth-two threshold circuit on \(x\in\{0,1\}^{n}\) consists of any finite number \(s\) of such gates applied to the original input bits, followed by one threshold output gate applied to their outputs. Arbitrary fan-in, fan-out and length-dependent weights are permitted; omitted inputs can have weight zero. Its size is \(s+1\), the number of threshold gates, not total weight magnitude or the number of bits encoding weights. Constants and direct input-to-output connections can be represented by additional threshold gates, changing size by at most \(n+1\), which does not alter exponential-size existence. Computation must agree with \(f_n\) on every input, with no approximation. The family is explicit in the definition of Section 1.5.1 of the source: there exist a polynomial \(q\) and a single deterministic polynomial-time verifier \(V\) such that \(f_n(x)=1\) precisely when some binary witness \(y\) with \(|y|\leq q(n)\) satisfies \(V(x,y)=1\). Verifier cost is measured on a standard bit Turing machine. Neither circuit weights nor circuits are required to be uniform or polynomially bounded. The exponential target is interpreted as \(2^{\Omega(n)}\) for all sufficiently large input lengths, with one fixed positive exponent coefficient.

context_blocks.text: Research Problem 11.40 asks for an exponential lower bound for unrestricted depth-two threshold circuits. The preceding discussion obtains strong bounds under restrictions on the weights; dropping such restrictions is the point of the question.

The source explicitly defines “explicit” in Section 1.5.1 through polynomial-time verification, corresponding to NP. Requiring the chosen function to lie in P would add a stronger condition that is not imposed here. Counting the existence of hard truth tables without this uniform verification condition would miss the intended explicit lower bound.

Chen’s 2018 paper describes even superpolynomial unrestricted depth-two threshold lower bounds for NEXP as a major frontier and develops conditional implications. Those implications do not supply the unconditional exponential lower bound for an NP family required by this card.

answer_criterion: Give a complete Lean-checked proof by specifying one uniform NP verifier defining the family and proving the stated exponential gate lower bound for every sufficiently large length, or prove that no such NP family and constants exist. A counting argument without an NP witness family, a bound on total weight, a restriction on signs or magnitudes, or a conditional complexity consequence does not meet the full target.

notes: Recovered the source-wide definition of explicit = NP, avoiding the unjustified stronger requirement that the function be computable in P.
Defined arbitrary signed real weights, exact gate semantics, two layers, gate-count cost and uniform verifier; the inner-product example preceding the question was not imposed as the required target.
Recorded the conventional interpretation of exponential as 2^{Omega(n)} eventually; retained the unrestricted source model and distinguished conditional later progress.
